policy: The S-stars whose orbits weigh Sagittarius A*, with orbital elements and physical values from the cited papers, and the red supergiant GCIRS 7 of the central parsec. An S-star shares the black hole's plotted position and system astrometry, because its orbit, well under a light-year across, is part of the system; GCIRS 7 is placed at the black hole's distance in its own direction, because its depth along the line of sight is unmeasured.

companions.name: S2
companions.note: The best-measured star around the black hole: a young B dwarf (B0–B3 V; log g = 4.10, v sin i = 110 km/s, m_K = 14.1). Mass 13.6 +2.2/−1.8 M_sun is its evolutionary initial mass, stored as the larger side of the interval; the temperature interval is +2388/−2923 K.

orbit.scope: Osculating elements of the four-star fit with M = 4.297e6 M_sun and R0 = 8277 pc, converted at 2010.35, near the star's apocenter. The physical axis converts the angular axis at that R0; the period follows from Kepler's third law with that mass.

companions.name: S29
companions.note: Passed the black hole in 2021 at about 100 AU and 8740 km/s, the closest approach GRAVITY has measured. m_K = 17.6: GRAVITY Collaboration 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.07478.

companions.name: S38
companions.note: One of the four stars whose orbits fix the black hole's mass and distance. m_K = 18.3: GRAVITY Collaboration 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.07478.

companions.name: S55
companions.note: A shorter orbit than S2's, reported in 2012 as S0-102. m_K = 17.2: GRAVITY Collaboration 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.07478.

companions.name: S4716
companions.note: Orbital period 4.02 ± 0.08 years, the shortest known when reported in 2022; pericenter 99 ± 8 AU. Spectral type B8/9 V and m_K = 17.02 ± 0.22: Peißker et al. 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02142.

orbit.scope: Maximum-likelihood (MCMC) Keplerian fit; the axis is published in milliparsecs and the period in the text (Section 3.6).

stars.name: GCIRS 7
stars.distance_note: 8277 pc, the distance of Sagittarius A* (GRAVITY Collaboration 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.07478); the star lies about 6 arcseconds, 0.24 pc in projection, north of the black hole, and its depth along the line of sight is unmeasured
stars.temperature_note: the mean over its pulsation, ± 195 K
stars.luminosity_note: 187,000 L_sun from the mean M_bol = −8.44 ± 0.22 with M_bol,sun = 4.74
stars.radius_note: Radius 960 ± 92 R_sun from the 2013 H-band uniform-disk diameter of 1.076 ± 0.093 mas at 8.33 kpc.
stars.note: Pulsating M1 red supergiant of the central parsec (2MASS m_K = 6.503 ± 0.017), with periods near 470 days and 2700–2850 days. Paumard et al. 2014 give an initial mass of 22.5 ± 2.5 M_sun and an age of 6.5–10 Myr; no present mass is adopted.
